# @celo/buy

`buy` pays HTTP `402 Payment Required` challenges with USDC, USDT or USAT on Celo.
It signs with a wallet held in your OS keychain, retries the request with an
`X-PAYMENT` header, and can attach a Self.xyz proof when an endpoint requires one.

Node.js 22 or newer is required. No clone, npm login, or global install is needed.

## Quickstart

### Sandbox: try it with no money

`--sandbox` runs the whole flow on Celo Sepolia with test USDC, and needs no setup.

```sh
npx --yes @celo/buy@0.8.5 --sandbox curl https://gateway.usebuy.ai/v1/social/x/posts/search \
  -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"query":"celo"}'
```

On the first run `buy` creates an account named `sandbox` on Celo Sepolia (no prompt,
never made your default), sees that it holds no USDC, asks the gateway's faucet
(`POST /v1/sandbox/fund` on the same origin) to fund it with 1 test USDC, waits for the
transfer to land, and pays the `celo-sepolia` offer. Two lines on stderr say what happened:

```
created sandbox account 0x… on celo-sepolia (test funds only)
sandbox: funded 0x… with 1 USDC (tx 0x…)
```

Later runs reuse the account and only call the faucet when it runs short. Sandbox USDC has
no value, and sandbox spend is kept off the account's mainnet daily cap. `buy --sandbox
whoami` shows the sandbox wallet once a paid call has created it (it never creates one itself);
`--account <name>` with `--sandbox` pays from that account on Celo Sepolia instead. The faucet
grants 1 USDC per address per day, so an offer above that cannot be paid from the sandbox. A server that offers mainnet only says so: drop `--sandbox` to pay
with real funds, or run your own gate with `buy gate --sandbox`.

Set `BUY_SANDBOX_NO_FUND=1` to never call the faucet; an empty wallet then fails the balance
check as on mainnet, pointing at <https://faucet.circle.com> (select "Celo Sepolia").

### Mainnet

Create a dedicated wallet. Celo mainnet is the default network:

```sh
npx --yes @celo/buy@0.8.5 setup --name demo
```

To pay from a wallet you already control instead — one you have declared to a programme
or allowlist, say — add `--import` and supply the raw hex private key in `BUY_IMPORT_KEY`
or on stdin (never as an argument, which would land it in shell history). `buy whoami`
then marks the account `(imported key)`. Encrypted keystore files are not supported.

Fund the printed address with a small amount of USDC, USDT or USAT on Celo mainnet. The
gateway sponsors transaction gas, so the buyer does not need CELO — and `buy send` pays its
gas in the token being sent (CIP-64), so moving money back out needs none either.

Create a Self proof if you plan to buy an `e2-standard-*` machine — the shared-core
sizes (`e2-micro`, `e2-small`, `e2-medium`) need none. Scope `buy.celo`, minimum age
18, and OFAC screening are defaults; the gateway verifies against the Self mainnet
hub, so a real passport is required and mock proofs are rejected:

```sh
npx --yes @celo/buy@0.8.5 verify hosted \
  --endpoint https://usebuy.ai/self/api/verify
```

The gateway hosts the Self receiver, so nothing listens on this machine and no
`cloudflared` is needed. The `--endpoint` is whatever the 402 challenge pinned —
a failed `buy curl` prints the whole command with it filled in, which beats
typing it. Against a gateway that pins no endpoint, use `verify serve` instead;
that one hosts a receiver locally and does need `cloudflared`.

Neither command ever receives the wallet private key.

Buy a one-hour `e2-micro` VM and run a script. Preserve the response because its
poll URL is the capability used to collect the result:

```bash
(
  umask 077
  set -o pipefail
  response_file=$(mktemp ./buy-vm.XXXXXX) || exit
  npx --yes @celo/buy@0.8.5 --verbose curl \
    --max-amount 0.02 \
    -X POST \
    --data '{"script":"uname -a; nproc","machineType":"e2-micro"}' \
    https://usebuy.ai/google/vm | tee "$response_file"
  response_status=$?
  printf 'Private response saved to %s\n' "$response_file" >&2
  exit "$response_status"
)
```

On Windows, write the body to a file and pass `--data-file body.json` in place of
`--data '{…}'`: PowerShell 5.1 corrupts an inline JSON argument (npm's `buy.ps1` shim
re-splits it, and `Out-File` prepends a UTF-8 BOM the gateway rejects as invalid JSON).
`buy curl` reads the file itself, strips a leading BOM, and gives curl a clean copy on
both the probe and the paid retry. Write the file as UTF-8 (`Out-File -Encoding utf8`; its
BOM is fine): PowerShell 5.1's default for `Out-File` and `>` is UTF-16, which `buy`
refuses with a hint rather than sending. `--data-file -` reads stdin to completion before
the first request. It cannot be combined with curl's own `-d`/`--data*`/`--json`/`-F`/`-T`;
`buy fetch` accepts the same option. Keep stdout and stderr separate (`2>&1` interleaves the error
envelope with the response), and pass curl's `--ssl-no-revoke` if Schannel reports a
certificate-revocation failure.

`--verbose` (before `curl` — after it, `-v` is curl's own flag) reports the
quote, the signing step and the settlement tx on stderr, one `{"log":"…"}` object
per line whenever stdout is not a terminal, so the `tee` above keeps the body and
the terminal keeps the tx hash.

The response contains a `poll` URL. Call it until `scriptStatus` is `done`; polling
is free:

```sh
npx --yes @celo/buy@0.8.5 curl '<poll-url>'
```

USDC is the default payment token. Add `--token USDT` or `--token USAT` to the paid command
to pay in one of those instead; a server must offer that token in its 402 for the payment to go through.

## Limits and safety

The public service uses on-demand VMs in `us-west1` and supports `e2-micro`,
`e2-small`, `e2-medium`, `e2-standard-2`, `e2-standard-4`, and `e2-standard-8`.
Quotes are authoritative. The service limits leases to one hour at a time and 24
hours total, admits at most 100 VMs, and stops admission at $25/hour of catalogued
compute. Each VM may send at most 10 GB of network egress; one that sends more
is deleted within minutes, and its lease is not refunded; its poll URL then reports
`egressCapExceeded: true`. `/google/ssh` is enabled and priced identically to `/google/vm` for the
same machine type.

Mainnet payments are real and irreversible. Use a dedicated low-balance wallet and
always set `--max-amount`. Do not automatically retry `500 provision_failed` or
`500 settle_uncertain`; settlement may already have occurred. A `4xx` or `503`
refusal happens before settlement.

`buy receipts --account demo` lists local payment history, including the settlement
transaction and, for a VM purchase, the poll URL. A receipt does not keep the response
body, instance, IP, or correlation ID, so keep the generated private response file until
the lease ends; a missing recovery field is not a reason to pay again. After a paid request
that ended without a 2xx, such as `500 settle_uncertain`, `buy receipts --resolve` asks
the token contract whether the payment settled.

## Other commands

```sh
npx --yes @celo/buy@0.8.5 --help
npx --yes @celo/buy@0.8.5 whoami
npx --yes @celo/buy@0.8.5 mcp install --client all
```

`buy quote` takes the same arguments as `buy curl` and stops at the 402: it prints
each offer's token, price, network, recipient and whether a Self.xyz attestation
is required, without a wallet and without paying. `--json` emits the raw envelope.
A route that answers anything other than 402 exits 1 with `unexpected_response`.

Wallet configuration and receipts persist between `npx` invocations. `BUY_HOME`
chooses a different data directory. Existing installations continue to use
`~/.config/cpay` (legacy default) and the existing OS-keychain entry, whose service name is
`cpay` (kept so the rename does not strand a wallet; `buy setup` prints it). `buy fetch` remains
the compatibility alias; new usage should prefer `buy curl`.

This is pre-1.0 beta software without an external security review. It is not
intended for production use.
